problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+4y-6z=4 \\ 6x+12y-18z=12 \\ -10x-20y+30z=-20\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Reduced Row Echelon Form of a Singular 3x3 System With One Pivot
examples.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-6y+2z=8 \\ -6x+18y-6z=-24 \\ 4x-12y+4z=16\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
examples.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14041946/assets/64b09692fa9522b79d0a8d481b4c997733bc5643cb56d2bc66eadce36d7bcc21.png)

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & 2 & 8 \\ -6 & 18 & -6 & -24 \\ 4 & -12 & 4 & 16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 4 \\ -6 & 18 & -6 & -24 \\ 4 & -12 & 4 & 16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+6{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 4 & -12 & 4 & 16\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-4){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

feedback.problem:
Consider the following system of linear equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}-2x-5y+2z=-7 \\ x+3y-z=5 \\ x+3y-z=5\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard Gauss-Jordan method to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to reduced row echelon form.
feedback.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & 2 & -7 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$

Transforming $M$ to reduced row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & -5 & 2 & -7 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 & 5 \\ -2 & -5 & 2 & -7 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 5\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

In the row echelon form above, we have only two pivots (in the $1$st and $2$nd columns). To transform the matrix to reduced row echelon form, we need to create zeros above the pivots only. This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :={R}_{1}-3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
